newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian budget to help villages see the light.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian budget to help villages see the light.

text.p: Indonesia plans to provide thousands of villages with electricity under its 1997/98 state budget starting April which has allocated 4.4 trillion rupiah to the mining and energy sector, President Suharto said on Monday.
The allocation is up from 4.10 trillion rupiah in the current 1996/97 budget.
He said almost all of the funds would be concentrated in the energy sub-sector, especially to support power generation, among others, for rural electrification.

"In 1997/98, more than 5,200 villages will have electricity. Thus, since the first 25-year-long development programme, more than 47,000 villages have enjoyed electricity or three-fourths of villages all over the country," he said.
Suharto said the tourism, post and telecommunications sector would be allocated more than 960 billion rupiah, down from 1.04 trillion in fiscal 1996/97.
"The reduced budget is caused by the greater participation of the public in the development of this sub-sector and the diminishing amount of foreign aid," he said.
He said, however, the budget for the tourism sub-sector was raised by 34 percent. The allocation rose to 69.4 billion rupiah from 51.8 billion in 1996/97.

Suharto said the government would allocate funds for the installation of 700,000 new telephone lines and the construction of telecommunication transmission networks to increase linkage between the various regions of the sprawling archipelago.
Allocation to the post and telecommunications sub-sector has been reduced to 893.3 billion rupiah from 991.5 billion rupiah in 1996/97.
